questions.question: Vinod talks about the only planet with liquid water on the surface. Which of the following planets is he talking about?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Earth is the only known planet that has stable water bodies on its surface and is called the "Blue Planet". Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
• Nearly 71% of the Earth is covered by water out of which 97.5% of Earth’s water is in the oceans, 2.75% is freshwater.
 
• Though Earth is an abundant source of water, still there is a shortage of fresh water because **99.7% of the water on the Earth is in the oceans, soils, icecaps, and floating in the atmosphere and only 0.3% is available for necessities.**
 
• **Water can exist in the air as water vapour, in rivers, lakes and glaciers, and in the ground as soil moisture.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Venus is the second planet from the Sun and is an inner planet and is sometimes referred to as Earth's twin planet** because of its similar size and density.

 
 
• On Venus, the solar wind strikes the upper atmosphere and carries off particles into space and because of it, **Venus has lost the majority of its water over the four and a half thousand million years.**
 
 
 
• **Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and is called a Red Planet because of its Iron minerals and rusty surface**.
 
 
• Many years ago, Mars had rivers but by **today no water body exists on it.**
 
 
 
• **Saturn is the sixth and second largest planet in the solar system and the only planet to have rings**.
 
 
• It is made up of Hydrogen and Helium.
 
• **It has an atmosphere that has traces of water but it does not have stable water bodies.**

questions.question: In October 2022, ISRO chairman announced expected launch year of Chandrayaan 3 in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ISRO chairman **announced that **Chandrayaan 3** is expected to be launched in **2023, **which is **two years later **than its initial planned launch year of **2021.**
 
• **Chandrayaan 3** is the** third lunar exploration mission** by the **Indian Space Research Organisation** (ISRO).
 
• It is aimed at conducting further studies on the **Moon's surface**, particularly in the **south polar region**, where** water molecules **have been detected.
 
• **Option 1**, i.e., 2030, is** incorrect** as it is too far away from the expected launch year.
 
• **Option 2**, i.e., 2027, and **option 3,** i.e., 2025, are also **incorrect** as they are not the exact launch year announced by the ISRO chairman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The previous **Chandrayaan missions, **Chandrayaan 1 and Chandrayaan 2, were launched in **2008 and 2019**, respectively.
 
• Chandrayaan 1 was India's **first lunar mission**, which discovered **water molecules** on the Moon's surface.
 
• Chandrayaan 2 aimed to make a** soft landing on the Moon's south polar region** but had a **communication failure** during the final stages of landing.

questions.question: Which country launched the first artificial satellite Sputnik 1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__USSR.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union/USSR sent the first artificial satellite 'Sputnik-1' into space.**
 
• The satellite was able to complete the orbiter of the** Earth in 96.2 minutes at a speed of 29000 kilometres per hour**.
 
• At the time of launch, it weighed around** 83.6 kg. Its diameter was 58 cm.**
 
• Sputnik was made like a metal ball and had four antennas.
 
• Sputnik-1 was giving signals of **20.005 and 40.002 MHz.**
 
• Sputnik-1, which signals to radio operators around the world, stopped working in just 21 days.
 
• **On 26 October 1957**, it stopped working due to its battery running out.
 
• The Sputnik 1 spacecraft was the first artificial satellite successfully placed in orbit around the Earth and was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome at Tyuratam (370 km southwest of the small town of Baikonur) in Kazakhstan, then part of the former Soviet Union.

questions.question: The substances which reduce friction are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lubricants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lubricants:-**

 
 
• **These are substances that are introduced between two surfaces in contact in order to reduce friction. (Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• They do this by forming a thin layer between the surfaces, which prevents them from rubbing directly against each other.
 
• This reduces the amount of heat generated and the wear and tear on the surfaces. 
 
• There are many different types of lubricants, including:
 
 
• Oils
 
• Greases
 
• Solids, such as graphite and molybdenum disulfide
 
• Liquids, such as water and silicone
 
• Gases, such as air and nitrogen
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluids:-**

 
 
• **These are substances that can flow easily and continuously deform under an applied shear stress, or external force. **
 
• They have zero shear modulus, or, in simpler terms, are substances which cannot resist any shear force applied to them.
 
 
 
• **Magnet:-**
 
 
• **It is a material or object that produces a magnetic field. **
 
• This magnetic field is invisible but is responsible for the most notable property of a magnet: a force that pulls on other ferromagnetic materials, such as iron, steel, nickel, cobalt, etc. and attracts or repels other magnets.
 
 
 
• **Spring:-**
 
 
• **It is an elastic object that stores mechanical energy and releases it when the opposing force is removed. **
 
• Springs can be made from a variety of materials, including metal, plastic, and rubber.
 
• They come in all shapes and sizes, and can be used in a wide variety of applications.

questions.question: What is the full form of INSAT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Satellite System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **INSAT** stands for **Indian National Satellite System**, a series of multipurpose geostationary satellites commissioned by ISRO.
 
• The primary objective of INSAT is to cater to telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and search and rescue operations.
 
• INSAT was established in 1983, marking a significant step in India's space program.
 
• These satellites are a collaborative effort between ISRO and the Department of Space, Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geostationary Satellites:**

 
 
• These are satellites that orbit the Earth at a fixed position relative to the surface, providing consistent coverage over a specific area.
 
• They are typically used for communication, weather forecasting, and surveillance.
 
 
 
• **ISRO:**
 
 
• The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is the space agency of the Government of India, responsible for the country's space program.
 
• ISRO's primary objective is to advance space technology and use its applications for various national tasks.
 
 
 
• **Telecommunications:**
 
 
• INSAT satellites play a crucial role in providing telecommunication services, including telephone and data transmission.
 
• They support the infrastructure for mobile networks, internet services, and direct-to-home (DTH) television.
 
 
 
• **Meteorology:**
 
 
• INSAT satellites are equipped with meteorological payloads to monitor weather patterns and provide crucial data for weather forecasting.
 
• They help in tracking cyclones, assessing rainfall, and predicting natural disasters.

questions.question: Which among the following planets does not have any satellite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jupiter:**

 
 
• **Jupiter** is the **largest planet in our solar system and it has the most number of confirmed moons as well. **
 
• The four largest, known as the **Galilean moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto), were discovered by Galileo Galilei in the early 17th century.**
 
 
 
• **Venus:**
 
 
• **Venus,** the second planet from **the sun** and our closest planetary neighbor, has **no natural moons**.
 
• While** Venus** is similar to **Earth in size and structure**, the lack of a moon is one of the many differences between the two planets.
 
 
 
• **Saturn:**
 
 
• **Saturn** is known for its extensive ring system, but it also has a large number of moons.
 
• Saturn has **145 confirmed moons**, the largest of which, **Titan,** is the second-largest moon in the solar system and is larger than the planet Mercury.
 
 
 
• **Uranus:**
 
 
• Uranus, the seventh planet from the Sun, has **27 known moons.**
 
• The names of all of the moons of Uranus are chosen from characters in the works of William Shakespeare and Alexander Pope.

questions.question: JJ Thomson is known for developing which model in 1898?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plum Pudding Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• J.J. Thomson proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** of the atom in 1898 after his discovery of the electron in 1897.
 
• According to this model, the atom is composed of a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it, resembling a "plum pudding."
 
• The model suggested that the positive charge is uniformly distributed throughout the atom, balancing the negative charge of the electrons.
 
• It was the first model to include the electron, an important step in understanding atomic structure.
 
• This model was later disproved by Ernest Rutherford’s Gold Foil Experiment in 1909, which led to the discovery of the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron Discovery:**

 
 
• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through his experiments with cathode rays.
 
• This discovery established that atoms are divisible and contain smaller subatomic particles.
 
 
 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:**
 
 
• In 1909, Ernest Rutherford conducted the Gold Foil Experiment, which demonstrated that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
 
• This experiment invalidated the Plum Pudding Model, leading to the Nuclear Model of the atom.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Model Evolution:**
 
 
• The Plum Pudding Model was an early attempt to explain atomic structure but lacked experimental support for the arrangement of charges.
 
• It was followed by Rutherford’s Nuclear Model and later by Niels Bohr’s Planetary Model.
 
 
 
• **Modern Atomic Theory:**
 
 
• The current understanding of atomic structure is based on quantum mechanics, incorporating the wave-particle duality of electrons and probabilistic electron clouds.
